title: a native pin whose graph reaches a host module two re-export hops away fails to compile, and the route names both hops
notes: specification/compatibility.mdx, 'Native Pin': the assertion is over the COMPLETE TRANSITIVE GRAPH, so a requirement reached through another module is the same requirement, and 'The diagnostic SHOULD show the dependency path that introduced the requirement.' `Module<"node:fs">` is poc/src/targets/classify.ts's concrete spelling of the JavaScript-host dependence that page names, and `blocksNativePin` refuses `TypeScript`, `Module<...>` and `Host<...>` together. `messageContains` pins the route because a pin refused with an empty route satisfies a code-and-position expectation exactly. The SMITHERS1510 companion lands in the auxiliary module, at the edge that reaches `node:fs`, because a re-export runs the target module's initializer exactly as an import does; it is declared rather than filtered because a cascade the language really does produce is part of the contract (conformance/README.md). Two hops, because following one re-binding and stopping is a distinct implementation from following until the binding is no longer a re-binding. The declared route names both modules in order, so a walk that reported only the module it was handed would fail here while still refusing the program. RETIRED MARKER (go, 2026-08-23): the fork used to accept this program, grant the pin and print `9` — zero diagnostics where the reference reports SMITHERS1510@1:30 in chain-inner-host-module.mod.sm and SMITHERS3001@15:1 in the case. The fork now advances one immediate checker alias at a time until the binding is no longer a re-binding (`nativeLaunderWalk`, compiler/forkbridge/nativepin.go.txt), so it names both hops: it satisfies the declared route `-> chain-outer-host-module.mod.sm -> chain-inner-host-module.mod.sm -> node:fs`, which a walk that followed one re-binding and stopped would not. Measured XPASS on go by `node conformance/runner/run.mjs --backend both --jobs 4`.
